records.claim: PCEM enables high contrast imaging of the interaction strength of cells with a surface, providing a specific attachment footprint as opposed to a generalized shape of the entire three-dimensional cell body.

records.claim: PCEM demonstrates that cell-surface attachment strength is not uniformly distributed within a cell or static as a function of time, but contains rich dynamic information including the rate of cell boundary extension, the size of a cell 'footprint' on a surface, and the effect of the extracellular environment on cell attachment.
records.quote: PCEM clearly demonstrates that cell-surface attachment strength is not uniformly distributed within a cell or static as a function of time, but instead contains rich dynamic information that includes the rate of cell boundary extension, the size of a cell "footprint" on a surface, and the effect of the extracellular environment (including chemotactic gradients) on cell attachment.

records.claim: PCEM enables continuous monitoring of spatial gradients in cell-surface attachment and the extension of fine-structured filopodia over extended time periods compatible with biological time scales of chemotaxis, apoptosis, differentiation, and proliferation, as a label-free detection approach.
records.quote: As a label-free detection approach, PCEM enables continuous monitoring of these phenomena over extended time periods that are compatible with the biological time scales of chemotaxis, apoptosis, differentiation, and proliferation.

records.claim: This work demonstrates, to the authors' knowledge, the first time-lapse movies of cell-surface interaction monitoring at biological time scales of chemotaxis, apoptosis, differentiation, and proliferation.
